key_insight: The paper provides a principled computational framework—grounded in control and game theory—that models and predicts co-adaptive dynamics between human users and decoders in closed‑loop neural interfaces, enabling design choices that reliably shape interaction outcomes.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a principled, predictive model for human–machine co‑adaptation in closed‑loop neural interfaces, which has led to unpredictable learning dynamics, poor usability, and suboptimal personalization of decoders.
method: Formulate users and decoders as interacting dynamical agents with separate objectives using control- and game-theoretic models.
Analyze stability and convergence of co‑adaptive trajectories to predict outcomes under different adaptation rules and parameter settings.
Use simulations and design prescriptions (e.g., update rules, regularizers, controller gains) to steer interactions toward desirable, personalized behaviors.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners principled tools to predict and shape learning dynamics in closed‑loop systems, improving robustness, personalization, and interpretability of neural interface algorithms.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the closed‑loop co‑adaptive system showing user ↔ decoder feedback loop with labeled objectives
Phase/trajectory plot showing convergence vs divergence regimes under different adaptation rates
Heatmap or bar chart comparing performance/usability metrics across decoder update rules and regularizers
Flowchart summarizing design pipeline: model → analysis → simulation → algorithmic prescription
paper_title: Computational framework to predict and shape human–machine interactions in closed-loop, co-adaptive neural interfaces
paper_authors: Maneeshika M. Madduri, Momona Yamagami, Si Jia Li, Sasha Burckhardt, Samuel A. Burden
